doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Three Deuces in Chicago and Zutty Singleton handing Hinton to Cab Calloway
summary: Hinton, working at the Three Deuces with Zutty Singleton and Art Tatum, is looked over by Calloway, who asks Zutty for him; he calls his mother at 3 am.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I know, I know. Deuces was the best gig.
That’s right that’s where it was, the Deuces —
That’s right. And Fletcher Henderson was at the Grand Terrace, $35 a week, with John Kirby on bass, trumpet player.

Chu Berry. And they was always looking for a jam session. After they got through at the Grand Terrace they’d come down to the Three Deuces and jam with us. So Cab came down to the Three Deuces and saw the band down there, and he never said a word to me. He was all dressed up in a big cool tan coat and that derby and he was walking around and people say, “That’s Cab,” he walked over to Zutty and said something to Zutty, he says, “How’s that bass player?” So Zutty says, “He’s okay, this kid’s okay.” So Cab says, “Can I have him?” So Zutty says, “Yeah you can have him” and nobody asked me nothing. So they just gave me to Cab.
Zutty say, “Kid you’re going,” I say, “I’m going where?” He say, “Cab just asked me for you” in that New Orleans style, “Cab just asked me for you. You’re gone.”
He’s going, baby. He’s got it made.
